data.content_ref: inline:The target's cross-city modulator is empirically backwards. It claims arid cities have a larger nocturnal UHI because they have less vegetation, while humid/irrigated cities have a smaller gap. But arid cities (e.g., Phoenix) typically have a NEGATIVE or very small nighttime UHI in summer because irrigated vegetation and anthropogenic moisture drive strong latent heat flux, whereas humid cities have a LARGER nighttime UHI because evapotranspiration is already atmospherically limited, so urban-rural latent-heat differences collapse and other factors dominate. The target thus inverts the observed arid-vs-humid relationship.
